messages:
Maria Chen: Quick pass — uploaded the 'Eclipse' dark theme Figma file. Main asks: syntax token clarity, chart palette for multi-series dashboards, and table/grid contrast. Fig: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/eclipse-theme
Dan O'Neill: Nice direction. Two quick nits: table row dividers feel too faint at small sizes, and secondary text (muted) drops below 4.5:1 on 13px body copy.
Asha Patel: Agree on muted text. Also the inline code color (current teal) and string color (soft green) are too similar when you skim. Hard to scan at a glance.
Maria Chen: Good call. Goal is to hit AA for body and WCAG for code snippets where we can. I'm aiming to keep the background slightly warmer than pure #0b0b0b to avoid glow.
Kevin Liu: Proposal: increase token hue separation. Keywords -> #5AB2FF, strings -> #A6E89A, function names -> #E6C07B, comments -> #6C7280 (lower saturation). That should push perceived difference.
Sam - Prod UX: Chart-wise we need colors that are distinct at small legend swatches and also colorblind-friendly. Can we pick a palette with good pairwise distances?
DesignBot: Automated contrast report: header (16px bold) = 4.6:1, body (13px) = 4.2:1, code inline = 3.7:1. Recommended adjustments: body +8% lightness or swap to #E6EDF3 for body text.
Dan O'Neill: I'd rather adjust token colors than body text if possible. Token ops are the real issue in editors. Also add a slightly darker border on table cells: from 0.06 -> 0.12 alpha.
Asha Patel: Quick mock idea — make code background a hair darker and add a subtle 1px inset border. Example CSS: 
```
/* code block tweaks */
.token-keyword { color: #5AB2FF; }
.token-string { color: #A6E89A; }
pre, code { background: rgba(6,8,10,0.65); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.03); padding: 8px; border-radius: 6px; }
```
Kevin Liu: That looks reasonable. For charts I'll propose a 6-color palette (colorblind-safe): #FF6B6B (coral), #4ECDC4 (teal), #5568FF (indigo), #FFD166 (amber), #9B8CFF (lavender), #2E8B57 (forest). They stay readable on dark bg and differ in luminance.
Maria Chen: Nice — can we run those through grayscale to check separability? Also legends need a 12px label weight tweak — slightly bolder.
DesignBot: Palette grayscale separability test: coral vs amber low contrast on grayscale (possible issue). Suggest swapping amber for #FFC86B to increase luminance gap.
Sam - Prod UX: UX nit: hover states on chart points are currently +6px glow; feels noisy. Recommend subtle fill change + outline instead.
Dan O'Neill: +1 on hover outline. Also file-level suggestion: show an accessibility badge next to theme toggles in Console to surface whether current theme meets AA.
Maria Chen: Love that — implement a small status chip (AA / WCAG2.1) near the theme selector. I'll update the Figma and send a new link.
Asha Patel: Small copy tweak: change "Dark Mode" menu label to "Eclipse (Dark)" when deployed so customers see the variant name.
Kevin Liu: sgtm. Last visual nit: focus rings — use 2px solid #8BC1FF at 60% opacity, not shadow-only. Improves keyboard discoverability.
Maria Chen: Thanks team. I'll push an updated fig and a staging preview. @DesignBot can you re-run contrast after I upload? :thumbsup:
DesignBot: Got it — re-run queued. Preview deployed to staging: https://staging.redwood.ai/theme-preview/eclipse — tag me when new fig uploaded. :eyes:
